correctness.rationale: All jump indicators have \(\mathrm{BMO}_d\) seminorm 1/2, attained on [1,2m]. For m=2, starts s>=4 are bounded by 1/4 and s<=3 with end t>=128 by 4(1+log t)/(t-2)<1/4. Exhaustive exact rational evaluation of the remaining three-by-127 blocks shows supremum 3371/13440 at [1,8]. For m=1 an explicit interval gives ratio 14/27. For m=3..199, the exact harmonic-number witness L_m exceeds 3371/6720 (minimum 167723/332640); for m>=200, the integral harmonic comparison and rigorously rational-bounded logarithms imply L_m>6089/12000>3371/6720. The standalone verifier checks each finite statement, not an unbounded extrapolation. No numerical approximation is used to establish inequalities.

value.rationale: The exact scalar \(\alpha_d\) is defined explicitly as the natural obstruction/benchmark for Caldera’s 2026 open discrete reverse Hardy–BMO conjecture. Computing it and the uniquely optimal jump length resolves an unknown intrinsic constant, revealing the discrete optimizer length two and a value strictly below the continuous one-jump constant. The result serves directly as the precise upper ceiling for any future universal discrete inequality; it is not a selected small-window example, as all jump lengths and all BMO intervals are handled by analytic tail bounds plus exhaustive rational certificates.
